draft.title: Gallipoli
card: Gallipoli is a peninsula in the Ottoman Empire (now Turkey). The Allies, including Britain and France, wanted to open a sea route to Russia and knock the Ottomans out of the war.
On 25 April 1915, soldiers of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps (ANZAC) landed at a spot later called Anzac Cove. The Ottoman defenders held the high ground above the beach.
The landing did not go to plan. The troops were pinned down on steep, rough land, and the fighting turned into a long stalemate.
The Allies never took the peninsula. They withdrew in December 1915 after heavy losses on both sides, so the campaign failed.
draft.remember: Gallipoli was an Allied campaign against the Ottoman Empire that began with the landing on 25 April 1915 and ended in failure.

a.q: What was the main aim of the Gallipoli campaign?
opts: To open a sea route to Russia and defeat the Ottomans
To capture Berlin and end the war in Germany
To defend Australia from a Japanese invasion
To win back the Belgian coast from Germany
a.why: The Allies hoped to open a sea route to Russia and knock the Ottoman Empire out of the war. Germany was fought mainly in Europe, not on the Gallipoli peninsula.
a.clue: Think about who the Allies were fighting at Gallipoli.

b.q: Jarrah reads that the Gallipoli campaign ended in December 1915 with the Allies leaving. Why is it described as a failure?
opts: The Allies did not take the peninsula and withdrew
The Allies took the peninsula but lost many men
The Ottomans surrendered but the Allies still left
The landing on 25 April was cancelled
b.why: The Allies did not reach their goals and left without taking the peninsula. Heavy losses alone do not explain it, as the Ottomans also lost many men and held the ground.
b.clue: Who held the land when the fighting ended?

wants.brief: A map of the Gallipoli peninsula showing Anzac Cove, the Aegean Sea and the Dardanelles, with the landing place marked.
wants.why: It shows how steep ground and the position of the landing made the campaign hard.

a.best: To open a sea route to Russia and defeat the Ottomans

b.best: The Allies did not take the peninsula and withdrew

problems.detail: The card says the Allies withdrew in December 1915. The Anzac and Suvla areas were evacuated by 20 December 1915, but British and French troops left Cape Helles on 8–9 January 1916, so the campaign ended in January 1916. Say the Anzacs left in December 1915, or that the last Allied troops left in January 1916.
The stem says the campaign 'ended in December 1915 with the Allies leaving'. The full Allied evacuation finished in January 1916; only the Anzac (and Suvla) withdrawal was in December 1915.
The clue 'Think about who the Allies were fighting at Gallipoli' points to the Ottomans, and only the right option mentions them, so a student can pick it without knowing the aim.
